DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The confirmed diagnosis of PML is supported by the patient's severe immunosuppression (CD4 count of 56), the characteristic MRI findings of disseminated non-enhancing white matter lesions, and the negative CSF PCR for JC Virus which rules out other causes of demyelination in this context. The clinical presentation of subacute neurologic decline (weakness, gait instability, cognitive changes) is classic for this opportunistic infection affecting the central nervous system. Immediate initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART) to restore immune function is the critical next step.
